outcomes.original: Expected condition: Hours of operation limited to close by 11 pm or midnight, with no service after 2 am (state law already prohibits alcohol sales after 2 am). Basis: Bars in neighborhood commercial districts are routinely conditioned to close by midnight or 1 am to mitigate noise and pedestrian impacts. The Third Street Alcohol RUD does not impose a statutory hours limit, but the Planning Commission typically conditions bar hours in the CUA motion.
outcomes.note: The records do not state what conditions are routinely imposed, what state law prohibits, or what the Planning Commission typically does.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Exterior lighting and window transparency: provide outside lighting and keep advertising to no more than 33% of windows and clear doors, with a clear view of the interior from the sidewalk. Basis: This is a mandatory operating requirement for all liquor establishments in the Third Street Alcohol RUD under Planning Code § 249.62(b), in force since before 2022. It will appear as a condition in the CUA motion or as a note that it applies by statute.
outcomes.note: The record confirms the overlay district but does not provide the text of § 249.62(b) or the specific lighting and transparency requirements stated in the condition.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Sound limits: plans submitted with the building permit shall incorporate acoustical insulation and sound-proofing measures to control noise, and the operator shall keep doors and windows closed during recorded-music hours if the Planning Commission finds potential for noise complaints. Basis: The one dated CUA for a cannabis operation at 1719 Wallace Ave (151 meters, 2024) imposed a condition requiring acoustical insulation and sound-proofing; bars with recorded music often receive similar conditions, especially in mixed-use blocks with residential upstairs.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If the Planning Commission grants the CUA, wait out the 30-day appeal period before filing the ABC license application or the building permit. What to say: The CUA is not final until the 30-day appeal period expires with no appeal filed. If an appeal is filed, the Board of Supervisors will hold a hearing; if the Board upholds the Commission's approval, the CUA is final. Do not pay ABC fees or building permit fees until the CUA is final, or make the lease contingent on CUA approval with no appeal.
outcomes.note: The record mentions a 30-day appeal period exists but does not state the finality rules, appeal procedures, or requirement to wait before filing other applications.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the ABC Type 42 license with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, submitting the signed lease, the final CUA motion, and the seller's permit. What to say: State in the ABC application that the concept is a beer-and-wine bar with food service, and attach the CUA motion showing Planning's approval. ABC will refer the application to SF Planning and SFPD; Planning will respond that the CUA is granted, and SFPD will review for crime and nuisance history. Post the 30-day public notice at the premises as ABC requires. If the census tract is flagged for undue concentration, request a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors or Planning Commission at the same time as the CUA hearing, so the PCN letter is ready when ABC needs it.
outcomes.note: Records confirm Type 42 exists and local review is typical, but don't state the specific documents, ABC referral process, notice requirements, or PCN timing described.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the health permit application with SF Department of Public Health, including the menu, equipment list, and proof that a certified food safety manager is on staff. What to say: State that the bar will serve limited food (sandwiches, small plates) with a limited kitchen and grease interceptor. DPH will route the application to Planning; Planning will respond that the CUA is granted. Schedule the pre-opening inspection for after the space is fully set up, with hot water, hand sinks, sealed surfaces, and the grease interceptor installed. The health permit is issued after the inspection passes.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,570 to $16,600. Notes: This is the time to approval and government cost for the three approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per the 2026–27 fee schedule, catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization), health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000, catalog entry sf.health_permit), and building permit with change of use (14–120 days for DBI review once the CUA is final, estimated $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation, though the description states no tenant improvements so the lower end is more likely). The CUA timeline includes pre-application meeting, environmental review, 300-foot neighborhood notice, Planning Commission hearing, and the 30-day appeal period; it is the critical path. The ABC Type 42 license is not in the entitlement path because its status is insufficient information (the description does not say how the license will be obtained), but if it is a new license expect 60–120 days and $1,000–$1,600 per catalog entry ca.abc_type_42, overlapping with the CUA and running in parallel once the CUA is granted. The day range is the time to approval when these approvals are granted; it is not a time to a denial or a withdrawal. Total government cost (CUA, health, building, ABC, business registration, seller's permit, EIN, food safety manager cert, RBS training, sign permit, ASCAP/BMI licenses) is estimated at $5,500–$20,000; the operating timeline from CUA filing to opening is 6–12 months if the CUA is approved at the first hearing with no appeal.
